equation.units: D_P in cm^2/s; Mr = relative molecular mass of migrant (g/mol); T = absolute temperature (K); tau in K; A_P' dimensionless
equation.interpretation: Gives an upper-bound (overestimating) diffusion coefficient D_P*; JRC text states D_P <= D_P*. tau = 1577 K corresponds to an extra activation energy term (Welle/Fraunhofer: tau 1577 K for PET ~ E_A 100 kJ/mol).
equation.status: TRANSCRIBED. Constants 0.1351, 0.003, 10454 and A_P = A_P' - tau/T VERIFIED from JRC59476 Sec. 2.2.1 Eqs. Sanity check: DBP (Mr 278) in LDPE at 40 C gives D ~ 2e-8 cm2/s, the expected order of magnitude.

crank.source: JRC59476 Sec. 2.1.3, Eqs. (3)-(6), citing Crank J. (1975) The Mathematics of Diffusion, 2nd ed., Oxford.
crank.geometry: Polymer film/sheet of thickness d_P, one side in contact with a finite, well-mixed food volume V_F, other side impermeable; uniform initial concentration c_P,0; no food-side mass-transfer resistance.
crank.series_solution: m_F,t / A = c_P,0 * rho_P * d_P * (alpha / (1 + alpha)) * [ 1 - SUM_{n=1..inf} ( 2*alpha*(1 + alpha) / (1 + alpha + alpha^2 * q_n^2) ) * exp( - D_P * t * q_n^2 / d_P^2 ) ]
crank.roots: tan(q_n) = - alpha * q_n, q_n = non-zero positive roots
crank.equilibrium: m_F,inf / A = c_P,0 * rho_P * d_P * alpha / (1 + alpha)
crank.units_tip: With c_P,0 in mg/kg, rho_P in g/cm3 and d_P in cm, the product c_P,0*rho_P*d_P is in ug/cm2. Divide by (food mass per contact area) to get mg/kg food. EU convention 6 dm2 per kg food (Reg. 10/2011 Art. 17(2)).
crank.root_finding_tip: For alpha > 0 each root q_n lies in ((n - 1/2)*pi, n*pi); bisect f(q) = tan(q) + alpha*q in that interval. About 20-50 terms suffice except at very short times.
crank.MIC_inverse: JRC Eq. (6) rearranges the series to find the maximum initial concentration c_P,0 that keeps migration below the SML.

short_time_approximation.general: M_t / M_inf ~= (1 + alpha) * [ 1 - exp(T_F / alpha^2) * erfc( sqrt(T_F) / alpha ) ], with T_F = D_P * t / d_P^2
short_time_approximation.infinite_food_limit: m_F,t / A ~= 2 * c_P,0 * rho_P * sqrt( D_P * t / pi ), valid while m_F,t / m_F,inf < ~0.5 and alpha >> 1
short_time_approximation.status: UNVERIFIED in this session. Standard Crank (1975) short-time result; JRC59476 Sec. 2.1.4 explicitly does not include alternative approaches.

kpf_defaults.rule: Without specific data: K_P,F = 1 if the migrant is highly soluble in the food/simulant (worst case, complete transfer at equilibrium); K_P,F = 1000 if the migrant is poorly soluble in the food (e.g., lipophilic substance in aqueous food).
kpf_defaults.source_section: JRC59476 Sec. 2.2.2; same wording in Tables 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 ('1 for high solubility of migrant in food, 1000 for low solubility'). Confirmed as the only two JRC values by Brandsch et al. 2022, Molecules 27:121, https://doi.org/10.3390/molecules27010121

EU_simulants_Reg_10_2011_AnnexIII.C: ethanol 20% (v/v), alcoholic foods <= 20% and foods with organic ingredients that make them more lipophilic
EU_simulants_Reg_10_2011_AnnexIII.D1: ethanol 50% (v/v), alcoholic foods > 20% and oil-in-water emulsions (e.g., milk/dairy)
EU_simulants_Reg_10_2011_AnnexIII.D2: vegetable oil, foods with free fats at the surface

simulant_mapping.suggested_app_rule: Use K = 1 for food classes represented by D1/D2/95% ethanol (fatty, oily, dairy foods) and K = 1000 for lipophilic migrants (log Kow > ~3) in aqueous/acidic foods (A, B). For hydrophilic migrants use K = 1 for all foods. This mapping is common practice but the JRC text does not give a simulant-by-simulant list (Brandsch 2022 says the same).
simulant_mapping.supporting_fact: Brandsch et al. 2022 note 50% ethanol as the simulant for dairy and 95% ethanol as an alternative for vegetable oil. VERIFIED from https://mdpi-res.com/d_attachment/molecules/molecules-27-00121/article_deploy/molecules-27-00121.pdf

kpf_models.name: Huang & Jolliet 2019 combined QPPR (packaging-food Kpf and material-water Kmw)
kpf_models.citation: Huang L., Jolliet O. (2019). A combined quantitative property-property relationship (QPPR) for estimating packaging-food and solid material-water partition coefficients of organic compounds. Science of the Total Environment 658:493-500. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2018.12.062
kpf_models.equation: log K_pf = f(log Kow, EtOH-eq, T, material type) as a multiple linear regression; generic variant uses log Kow, EtOH-eq and T only (no material).
kpf_models.coefficients: UNVERIFIED. Paper is paywalled (ScienceDirect robots-blocked, ResearchGate fetch failed). Not retrieved.
kpf_models.performance: Material-specific model adj. R2 = 0.93; generic model adj. R2 = 0.90; external R2 > 0.80. Data: 1846 measured Kpf or Kmw for 232 chemicals in 19 consolidated material types.
kpf_models.applicability: Temperature range of the data 275-313 K; EtOH-eq 0-100% (per Vaferi et al. 2025 description of the same dataset).

microwave_temperatures.finding: Pork patties (90 g) in a microwaveable plastic container, 700 W domestic oven: edge temperature rose linearly to 100 C while other parts stayed below 80 C; minimum temperatures 52-88 C depending on patty type; simulated after 60 s: edge hot spot ~80 C vs centre cold spot ~50 C.
microwave_temperatures.source: Jung H., Lee M.G., Yoon W.B. (2022) Processes 10(11):2382, https://doi.org/10.3390/pr10112382 ; https://www.mdpi.com/2227-9717/10/11/2382

microwave_temperatures.finding: Olive oil heated for fast-food preparation reached about 140 C at ~9 min (figure covers both microwave and conventional heating; microwave oil temperature was lower than conventional).
microwave_temperatures.source: Mahmoud E.A.E.-M. et al. (2009) Czech J Food Sci 27 (Spec. Issue): S173-S177, https://www.agriculturejournals.cz/pdfs/cjf/2009/10/27.pdf

microwave_temperatures.finding: In a microwave the fat phase heats about twice as fast as water or water-containing foods under comparable conditions (cited Dostalova et al. 2005).
Hong Kong take-away container study: a PS container exceeded the overall migration limit with fatty food at 120 C but passed at 100 C; EPS/PS/PET judged unsuitable for food above 100 C.
microwave_temperatures.source: Centre for Food Safety Hong Kong (2005) Disposable Plastic Containers for Take-away Meals, https://www.cfs.gov.hk/english/programme/programme_rafs/programme_rafs_fc_01_03_dp.html

microwave_temperatures.finding: EU hot-fill definition: food filled at not more than 100 C, then cooled to <=50 C within 60 min or <=30 C within 150 min.

Aqueous foods/water cannot exceed ~100 C at atmospheric pressure, so the aqueous-food scenario is bounded at 100 C; fat-rich foods and food-container interfaces can exceed it. Castle et al. 1990 (Food Addit Contam 7(6):779-796) and Jickells et al. 1993 (Food Addit Contam 10(6)) measured microwave temperatures for plastics and olive oil, but their numbers were NOT retrieved.

Microwave migration experiment conditions in practice: 540 W oven, 30 s exposures followed by ice-water cooling; olive oil simulant referred to at 100 C; container thickness PS 1.7 mm, PP 1.2 mm, PET 0.5 mm (useful d_P defaults).
microwave_temperatures.source: Cai R., Mokwena Nthoiwa K.K., Ge C., J. Applied Packaging Research, https://repository.rit.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1004&context=japr

notes: Validity warning for the app: JRC validity T_max is 70 C for PS, HIPS, SBS and rigid PVC, 80 C for LDPE (as transcribed), 90 C for HDPE. Microwave reheating (~100 C, edges/fat >100 C) is outside the validated range for these polymers; PP (<=120 C) and PET/PEN (<=175 C) remain in range. The app should flag out-of-range cases.
Piringer gives an upper-bound (overestimate) D; with K_P,F = 1 the result is a conservative worst case, which is the intended EU use.
Parameter table is from JRC59476 (2010). The 2015 JRC98028 guideline could not be read (EPUB only; host blocked to the sandbox). UNVERIFIED whether any A_P'/tau value changed in 2015.

The '1,847 log Kpf values for 232 materials and 19 compounds' in earlier notes is the Huang & Jolliet 2019 dataset, re-used by Wang 2023, Vaferi 2025 and Wei 2025. Correct reading: 232 chemicals in 19 material types; part of the records are material-water Kmw, not Kpf.
The dataset's temperature range is only 275-313 K (2-40 C). Any Kpf ML model trained on it extrapolates when applied at microwave temperatures (~373 K).
